title: Verify a new anonymous user can complete the entire preference questionnaire and view personalized job results without registration
description: This test verifies the core 'happy path' for a new, anonymous user. It ensures the user can provide all their preferences and immediately see the value (personalized results) without any registration barrier, which is a key business goal. Automation feasibility: HIGH.
testDescription: As a new job seeker visiting the site for the first time, I want to provide my job preferences through a guided questionnaire so that I can see a relevant list of jobs without needing to create an account first.
prerequisites: User must be a new visitor with no existing cookies or session data for the platform. The platform has active job listings matching a variety of preferences.
stepsToPerform:
1. Open a new incognito browser window to simulate a first-time visit.
2. Navigate to the application's home page. Observe that the guided preference questionnaire is displayed.
3. Select 'Fully remote' for the 'working arrangement' preference.
4. Select 'Income' for the 'motivating the search' preference.
5. Enter a valid annual salary, e.g., '95000'.
6. Select a location, e.g., 'United States'.
7. Enter a job title, e.g., 'Senior QA Lead'.
8. Enter '7' for 'years of relevant experience'.
9. Complete all other available preference fields with valid data.
10. Click the 'Submit' or 'See Jobs' button at the end of the questionnaire.
11. Observe the job results page is loaded and displays relevant listings.
expectedResult:
1. The user is successfully redirected to the job results page.
2. A personalized set of job listings is displayed, filtered and ranked based on the preferences provided.
3. The user is not prompted to register or pay to view the results.
4. The session is maintained as anonymous.

title: Verify the system records which preferences were provided and which were left unanswered during a partial questionnaire completion
description: This test ensures the system correctly handles incomplete data submission from the questionnaire, which is crucial for accurate partial matching and for allowing users to complete their profile later. Automation feasibility: MEDIUM (may require API inspection to verify stored state).
testDescription: As a new job seeker who is in a hurry, I want to answer only the most important questions in the questionnaire and still get relevant results, with the system remembering which questions I skipped so I can answer them later.
prerequisites: User is a new visitor with no existing session cookies or account. The questionnaire UI allows skipping non-mandatory fields.
stepsToPerform:
1. Open a new incognito browser window.
2. Navigate to the application's home page and start the questionnaire.
3. Select 'Hybrid' for the 'working arrangement' preference.
4. Enter 'Project Manager' for the 'job titles' preference.
5. Deliberately skip the 'annual salary' and 'years of relevant experience' fields.
6. Select 'Technology' for the 'category or field' preference.
7. Skip all other optional fields.
8. Submit the partially completed questionnaire.
9. Observe the job results page.
10. Navigate to a 'My Preferences' or 'Edit Filters' section to inspect the saved state.
expectedResult:
1. The system generates job results based on the provided preferences ('Hybrid', 'Project Manager', 'Technology').
2. In the session data (verifiable via API or a 'My Preferences' UI), the provided preferences are stored correctly.
3. The session data explicitly records that 'annual salary' and 'years of relevant experience' were left unanswered (e.g., stored as null or an empty value).

sourceCitation.excerpt: Record which preferences were provided and which were left unanswered.

testDescription: A job seeker enters a very specific and rare combination of preferences, such as a high-level job title in a niche field, combined with a very high salary requirement and a location in a small town. 3. Submit the questionnaire and proceed to the job results page.
4. Observe the total number of results and verify it is very low (e.g., 'Showing 2 jobs').
